correctness.rationale: A direct discharging inequality on cubic graphs makes every transferred vertex weight at least 1/2; equality forces the explicit E+/E− neighbor patterns, which conversely satisfy all feasibility constraints. Even prisms admit weight-m alternating-column witnesses. A 256-state cyclic transfer counts precisely all equality labelings. An entirely specified integer computation yields recurrent SCC sizes \(22,4,4,4,2\), with core characteristic polynomial \(t^{14}(t^8-7t^4+1)\); power-sum identities prove the claimed all-even m formula. Reproducible integer certificate, independent optimum DP at \(m=4,6,8\) and brute-force m=4 check the premises. A finite test alone is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The number of optimizing four-label functions is a natural equality-case parameter for a published extremal graph family; known \(\gamma_{\mathrm{sdR}}=m\) and example witnesses do not furnish its multiplicity. The exact count identifies surprising rigidity (two optima for \(m\equiv2\pmod4\)) versus exponential growth (a Lucas-type recurrence at multiples of 4), and an equality transfer structural mechanism reusable in other constrained labeling problems.
